_status: PROPOSAL — nothing reads this yet. This is the corporate baseline for gap F-9: one SpatialCodeRegistry replacing the five level vocabularies and three LOC vocabularies that currently disagree. Ship it as StingTools/Data/STING_SPATIAL_CODES.json; project overrides land at <project>/_BIM_COORD/spatial_codes.json, merged by code, following the AecFilterRegistry pattern (Core/Drawing/AecFilterRegistry.cs:18-90).
_levelNote: The ISO 19650 UK Annex level field is TWO characters: ZZ = many levels, XX = no level, 00 = ground/base, then 01, 02 upward. STING's tag vocabulary instead uses GF and L01. Both are in here: 'code' is the STING tag code, 'isoCode' is what belongs in an ISO 19650 file name. Today these two live in different files and nothing reconciles them (gap F-6) — one entry per level fixes that. 'aliases' is what ParameterHelpers.GetLevelCode should match a Revit level NAME against, replacing its 80-line if-chain.

levels.label: Mezzanine 2
levels._note: The current parser returns MZ for every mezzanine, so a second one silently collides (gap F-4).

levels._generatorNote: L06-L99 follow the same shape. The registry should synthesise Lnn / nn on demand rather than enumerate 99 rows — the alias rule is 'level <n>' and the ordinal words.

levels.label: Plant level
levels._note: The current parser only matches when the name BOTH starts with 'plant' AND contains 'room' — so 'Plant Level' and 'Plantroom' both miss (gap F-4).

levels.label: Upper roof / parapet
levels._note: Emitted by the wizard's ProposeIsoLevelCode but not producible by GetLevelCode — one of the five-way vocabulary splits.

_locNote: The LOC vocabulary. Today this is hard-coded as BLD1/BLD2/BLD3/EXT in TagConfig.Defaults.cs:592-595 and again, differently, in LocVocabularyOverride (MultiBuildingCommands.cs:24-42), and extended by three separate config keys that do not agree (gap F-1). 'aliases' revives the dead TagConfig.LocPatterns idea (TagConfig.cs:1253-1258) — a name-to-code inference table that currently has zero consumers.
_projectTypeNote: This is the piece that makes the vocabulary per-project-type. SectorPack (Core/SectorPackCommand.cs:17-29) currently carries Families, Presets, TagStyle, PreambleProfile, BoqDefaults and WorkflowPresets — and NO spatial key, so a hospital and a data centre get identical level vocabularies. Adding one field and one line in Apply() lets each Data/SectorPacks/*_PACK.json name a block below.

HOSPITALITY.note: Lodges and resorts are typically single-storey pavilions on a shared site. Building codes are project-specific and come from the project override.

HEALTHCARE.note: Plant levels matter disproportionately in healthcare — PL must be first-class, not a parser accident.

DATACENTRE.note: Mezzanine and plant are the working levels; MZ2 is common and currently unrepresentable.

_kibaleOverride: For Kibale the project override file would carry the eleven cottage/facility LOC codes and just XX/ZZ/GF/RF as levels — see project_config.json in this folder for the equivalent expressed through today's three-key mechanism.
